evidence.summary: 在 DeepSeek Harness 中浏览社区插件，并管理安装、更新和配置。
limitations: 功能摘要根据作者固定版本材料归纳，不是逐字引文或独立效果验证。

evidence.summary: 核查 README.md、cordis.patch.yml、package.json、src/backup.ts、src/client/MarketSection.tsx、src/drain-journal.ts、src/drain.ts、src/dsh-cli.ts、src/http.ts、src/index.ts、src/install.ts、src/official-desktop.ts、src/pending-updates.ts、src/registry.ts、src/routes.ts；[Q02](#research-q02) 客户端选择→路由重新查目录→宿主包管理/CLI→盘面后验；[Q03](#research-q03) 来源/兼容与请求门有条件限制；[Q04](#research-q04) 通过排空、日志、备份和特定Desktop修复分担变更状态。
limitations: 固定根原生插件，实际读取客户端安装、入口/运行时、安装及代表更新卸载、目录/请求/兼容门、排空/取消、本地restore及Desktop中断更新修复。未全审主题/收藏/分组/排序、公共更新API、云备份/Gist讨论和detach重启页面。旧七题与全部findings已逐项重核。
只执行本工程的统计和结构验证；没有执行目标插件、测试、安装或真实宿主验收。
GitHub/npm 活跃度只作采集背景，未核实独立用户采用或同条件收益对照。

findings.text: [Q01](#research-q01) 面向重复维护多插件且能备份/修复profile的使用者；合格结果是目标插件与profile可加载，正在执行的任务不被变更破坏。
[Q02](#research-q02) 客户端选择→路由重新查目录→宿主包管理/CLI→盘面后验；[Q03](#research-q03) 来源/兼容与请求门有条件限制；[Q04](#research-q04) 通过排空、日志、备份和特定Desktop修复分担变更状态。
固定根原生插件，实际读取客户端安装、入口/运行时、安装及代表更新卸载、目录/请求/兼容门、排空/取消、本地restore及Desktop中断更新修复。未全审主题/收藏/分组/排序、公共更新API、云备份/Gist讨论和detach重启页面。旧七题与全部findings已逐项重核。
原生DSH插件：根导出服务、web客户端与bundle patch；1.73.12/MIT。当前Git包版本与缓存npm META的采集时间/最新版本不同，不把缓存当实时发行确认。

| 阶段 | 现金与资源 | 人工与状态负担 |
|---|---|---|
| 首次 | 下载/存储费未知 | profile与包信任核对、备份，分钟未知 |
| 持续 | 来源网络及目标包服务费未知 | 版本/兼容/凭据维护 |
| 失败恢复 | 重试资源及额外包费用未知 | 取消残留、部分恢复、重启修复上限需核 |
| 退出 | 退款/第三方用量另核 | 市场移除不等于其他包/禁用patch/凭据清理 |
[Q05](#research-q05) 在独立profile单包完成安装、更新、卸载和恢复，再与原生Discover/CLI比较；核来源、目录、实际激活和errors而非总ok。只在备份与手工救援可行时扩大；[Q06](#research-q06)的变更收据另作实验。

| 效果项 | 当前支持 | 未确认 |
|---|---|---|
| 安装结果 | 新增manifest/入口/冲突后验 | 同Host合格率与安全 |
| 活动任务维护 | 有条件Agent屏障 | 全宿主并发/外部CLI安全 |
| 故障状态 | 明确部分差异、终态日志、特定重试 | 原子恢复或全部自动自愈 |
| 采用收益 | 可控范围的隔离试用计划 | 节时、净收益与持续维护成本 |
[Q02](#research-q02) 不只信退出码，按盘面后验；[Q03](#research-q03)兼容/请求门存在条件；[Q04](#research-q04)disposed例外、mutation前重claim、终态日志与Desktop特定持久修复不能混淆。复杂恢复分支也带来维护与未验证风险，不以测试文件数或源码复杂度加分。
[Q02](#research-q02) 的精确目标重比、manifest/可加载入口/冲突后验，与[Q04](#research-q04) 实际Agent排空和有条件恢复构成可检查的插件维护组合。它比只信CLI退出码多给盘面和失败信息，但继承包管理器/Host能力，没有证明全事务恢复或实测节时。
[Q02](#research-q02) 集合部分成功、可覆盖的活动Agent确认和取消残留，[Q03](#research-q03) 未知兼容与缺gate放行，以及[Q04](#research-q04) 逐文件/部分恢复与重试上限，意味着一个成功标志不能证明整个profile已恢复且安全。集中操作是否值得，要看用户能否承担这些核对与救援成本。
[Q06](#research-q06) 候选是将批准目标、真实盘面/激活差异与可执行恢复组合成变更收据，在独立profile演练后审查迁移；以当前市场+备份作对照，若遗漏原环境故障、目标不可复现或人工恢复更多就推翻，尚未验证。

| 依赖 | 作用 | 版本或条件 |
|---|---|---|
| dshmarket | 本组件 | 1.73.12，MIT |
| DSH webServer/loader | 挂载服务 | README声明web>=0.1.0-rc.6，实际需验证 |
| Cordis/settings/schema | 宿主服务与配置 | Cordis^4.0.1；settings peer列rc.7/0.1.1/0.1.2/0.2系列且optional；schema^3.18.1 optional |
| js-yaml/undici | 配置/网络 | ^4.3.2 / ^7.29.1 |
| CLI/pnpm或Desktop manager | 真正包执行 | 正确profile目录、可用能力与下载网络 |
| Agent服务与事件 | 排空 | 可列举并订阅created/disposed、兼容maintenance |

technical.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)/[Q04](#research-q04)：novelty9是成熟目录、包管理、后验和maintenance组合的局部增量，超过仅包装0；未识别新方法到18。mechanism15以命令前reclaim/精确目标及盘面检查改变并发/假成功行为，超过薄接口8；取消残留、可覆盖确认和宿主差异未解决直接替代关键限制，不到23。transferability10可将批准目标重比和Agent维护屏障迁移其他宿主扩展维护，超过只用于此UI5；依赖Host事件/maintenance与布局，未证明多宿主一致，不到15。simplification4集中接线减少手工核入口，但引入大量恢复分支且无同负担更简洁证据，不到8，仍超只增加目录入口0。

business.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) 至 [Q05](#research-q05)：workflow0已比较Discover/CLI，仍是同一操作者选包/授权/修复，排空并非人员分工与交付责任变化，未到9。delivery8把单退出码扩成新增包/冲突/激活/部分错误结果，超过无改变0；仍交付同一插件profile且没有完整验收单元改变，不到15。reach0已有原生Discover GUI，同一人群无需此市场才能入场，不能按一键便利到5。economics0已核来源获取、包执行和备份/恢复，资源和责任仍由用户维护，未识别计价、供给或服务结构改变，不到4；总费未知另列成本，不作零分理由。

recommendation.reason: 经常维护多个社区插件并能修复 profile 的 DSH 使用者，可先备份配置、锁文件与凭据，在独立 profile 或可还原副本中试一组非关键包。市场把目标重比、安装后盘面校验和 Agent 排空接到包操作，比只看 CLI 退出码提供更多恢复线索，但部分成功和取消仍需人工核盘。遇到宿主身份或请求门不清、自动修复放弃、残留无法恢复就停止并回退备份或原生 Discover/CLI，唯一生产 profile 先不采用。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) 的多插件维护者及[Q02](#research-q02) 实际部分安装/更新/卸载、[Q04](#research-q04)恢复，具体解释重复变更误判如何影响启动，超一般用途15；无目标人群频次和同任务需求记录，不到30。

advantage.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02) routes与install真实后验、[Q04](#research-q04)命令前Agent屏障相对Discover同目录+CLI有可解释增量，超纯入口6；部分成功/取消与宿主差异使核心恢复收益仍不确定，不到19。

evidence.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)客户端→路由→实际spawn/manager→盘面、[Q03](#research-q03)门及[Q04](#research-q04)真实失败/恢复caller均覆盖，超片段声明6；尚无安装/Host测试与效果实验，不到19，只支持有条件试用。

cost.rationale: [Q05](#research-q05)可还原副本/备份提供有限退路，超无可行恢复0；[Q02](#research-q02)取消/部分安装与[Q04](#research-q04)跨文件补偿、部分恢复/修复放弃仍要求用户救援，未有完整可控恢复与退出数据，不到10。

publication.summaries.text: 在 DeepSeek Harness 中浏览社区插件，并管理安装、更新和配置。

items.界面: 在Host内选择目录条目、显示包变更和恢复信息。
items.Host 路由: 接收安装、更新、卸载和本地恢复请求并核条件。
items.后台: 调用宿主包管理器/CLI，后验盘面并协调兼容Agent排空。

publication.capabilities.table:
| 能力 | 主要用途 | 使用条件与边界 |

| 目录选择与安装 | 将条目送宿主包操作并核新增包 | 仅目录成员；不是代码安全审计 |
| 更新与卸载 | 管理活动profile中的插件版本/移除 | 部分成功、取消及宿主差异需核盘 |

| 本地恢复与特定修复 | 从备份/中断记录整理profile | 逐文件/部分恢复，非全局事务 |

data.reports:
# DSH Market > 在 DeepSeek Harness 中浏览社区插件，并管理安装、更新和配置。 ## 研究范围 - **仓库**：[dsh-market/dsh-market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) - **版本号**：1.73.12（[固定提交 19641d22a69b63063bb9b67a5f67a0dcb72703a0](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market/tree/19641d22a69b63063bb9b67a5f67a0dcb72703a0)） - **版本日期**：2026-11-06（固定提交日期，北京时间；不是包发布日期） ## 结论状态 固定源码支持有条件的变更治理组合；建议有备份和排障能力者隔离试用，未安装运行或真实宿主验收；变更收据方向未验证。 ## 洞察短评 - **用途**：[Q01](#research-q01) 面向重复维护多插件且能备份/修复profile的使用者；合格结果是目标插件与profile可加载，正在执行的任务不被变更破坏。 - **亮点**：[Q02](#research-q02) 的精确目标重比、manifest/可加载入口/冲突后验，与[Q04](#research-q04) 实际Agent排空和有条件恢复构成可检查的插件维护组合。它比只信CLI退出码多给盘面和失败信息，但继承包管理器/Host能力，没有证明全事务恢复或实测节时。 - **思考**：[Q02](#research-q02) 集合部分成功、可覆盖的活动Agent确认和取消残留，[Q03](#research-q03) 未知兼容与缺gate放行，以及[Q04](#research-q04) 逐文件/部分恢复与重试上限，意味着一个成功标志不能证明整个profile已恢复且安全。集中操作是否值得，要看用户能否承担这些核对与救援成本。 - **建议**：[Q06](#research-q06) 候选是将批准目标、真实盘面/激活差异与可执行恢复组合成变更收据，在独立profile演练后审查迁移；以当前市场+备份作对照，若遗漏原环境故障、目标不可复现或人工恢复更多就推翻，尚未验证。 采用建议：[Q05](#research-q05) 在独立profile单包完成安装、更新、卸载和恢复，再与原生Discover/CLI比较；核来源、目录、实际激活和errors而非总ok。只在备份与手工救援可行时扩大；[Q06](#research-q06)的变更收据另作实验。 ## 核心贡献 [Q02](#research-q02) 的精确目标重比、manifest/可加载入口/冲突后验，与[Q04](#research-q04) 实际Agent排空和有条件恢复构成可检查的插件维护组合。它比只信CLI退出码多给盘面和失败信息，但继承包管理器/Host能力，没有证明全事务恢复或实测节时。 ## 关键质疑 [Q02](#research-q02) 集合部分成功、可覆盖的活动Agent确认和取消残留，[Q03](#research-q03) 未知兼容与缺gate放行，以及[Q04](#research-q04) 逐文件/部分恢复与重试上限，意味着一个成功标志不能证明整个profile已恢复且安全。集中操作是否值得，要看用户能否承担这些核对与救援成本。 ## 重点创新推演与最小验证 [Q06](#research-q06) 候选是将批准目标、真实盘面/激活差异与可执行恢复组合成变更收据，在独立profile演练后审查迁移；以当前市场+备份作对照，若遗漏原环境故障、目标不可复现或人工恢复更多就推翻，尚未验证。 仅源码核查，未运行目标代码/测试、安装包、宿主/模型/浏览器或真实账号。未来隔离故障矩阵应核目标漂移、部分安装、disposed/hold丢失、取消、磁盘中断及恢复上限；需求/成本对照仍为明确缺口。 ## 场景与替代办法 [Q01](#research-q01) 面向重复维护多插件且能备份/修复profile的使用者；合格结果是目标插件与profile可加载，正在执行的任务不被变更破坏。 [Q01](#research-q01) 原生Discover可使用同一目录，CLI也能安装更新；本项额外价值应比较实际变更检查与恢复，而不是目录独占或GUI低门槛。 ## 依赖与流程 | 依赖 | 作用 | 版本或条件 | |---|---|---| | dshmarket | 本组件 | 1.73.12，MIT | | DSH webServer/loader | 挂载服务 | README声明web>=0.1.0-rc.6，实际需验证 | | Cordis/settings/schema | 宿主服务与配置 | Cordis^4.0.1；settings peer列rc.7/0.1.1/0.1.2/0.2系列且optional；schema^3.18.1 optional | | js-yaml/undici | 配置/网络 | ^4.3.2 / ^7.29.1 | | CLI/pnpm或Desktop manager | 真正包执行 | 正确profile目录、可用能力与下载网络 | | Agent服务与事件 | 排空 | 可列举并订阅created/disposed、兼容maintenance | | 步骤 | 操作 | 核对与失败处理 | |---|---|---| | 首次 | 核Host/profile/路径并备份 | 不能把web安装当Desktop已安装 | | 选择 | 比较原生Discover、来源和兼容 | unknown不当通过证明 | | 单包变更 | 安装/更新/卸载并看盘面/激活 | 集合ok不等于每包成功 | | 有任务时 | 停重要任务或用受支持drain | 普通确认字段不能当隔离 | | 恢复退出 | 核差异、备份和patch | 自动修复放弃即人工救援 | ## 成本与效果 | 阶段 | 现金与资源 | 人工与状态负担 | |---|---|---| | 首次 | 下载/存储费未知 | profile与包信任核对、备份，分钟未知 | | 持续 | 来源网络及目标包服务费未知 | 版本/兼容/凭据维护 | | 失败恢复 | 重试资源及额外包费用未知 | 取消残留、部分恢复、重启修复上限需核 | | 退出 | 退款/第三方用量另核 | 市场移除不等于其他包/禁用patch/凭据清理 | | 效果项 | 当前支持 | 未确认 | |---|---|---| | 安装结果 | 新增manifest/入口/冲突后验 | 同Host合格率与安全 | | 活动任务维护 | 有条件Agent屏障 | 全宿主并发/外部CLI安全 | | 故障状态 | 明确部分差异、终态日志、特定重试 | 原子恢复或全部自动自愈 | | 采用收益 | 可控范围的隔离试用计划 | 节时、净收益与持续维护成本 | ## 研究问题与完整回答 **插件研究总目标**：重复维护插件者何时能通过市场安全改变活动profile，何时应退回原生Discover/CLI？ ### Q01 · 谁需要额外市场，真实入口和原生 Discover 的边界是什么？ **研究主题**：场景与需求、贡献与相对优势 #### 完整回答 DSH Market 是原生 DSH 插件，根 dshmarket 版本 1.73.12、MIT；导出服务入口、bundle patch 与 web 客户端。apply 真正 inject webServer/loader 并挂载路由，不是独立桌面客户端。官方 Desktop 分支使用宿主 pluginManager，普通宿主则按显式配置、launcher、argv 再默认 web 选择 profile；同机安装到 web 不表示装到 Desktop。README 声明 web 最低 0.1.0-rc.6，package 的 settings peer 从 rc.7 等系列且 optional，不能把两个不同约束混成最低实际兼容证明。 目标是经常维护多插件、需要安装后核可加载入口并能恢复 profile 的用户，合格结果是目标包及活动 profile 可加载、任务未被中途文件修改破坏。基本搜索并非独占：作者明确同一目录索引能接进 DSH 0.2.1+ Discover；偶发安装可以使用原生 Discover 和 CLI，不能只因多一个市场页就认定任务组织发生创新。实际增量须落到以下各题的包变更、盘面后验、排空和恢复，而不是目录数量或受欢迎程度。 本轮完整复核正式前稿七题与全部 findings，检查当前入口、安装/代表更新/卸载、目录与请求门、Agent 排空、本地备份恢复及 Desktop 中断更新修复代表链。收藏/分组/主题、负载顺序、全部快照/同步/WebDAV/Gist、讨论外部账户、脱离宿主的重启恢复页面和公共更新 API 不在完整机制验收范围；作者列举这些功能不能自动当本轮已验证能力。 #### 证据与依据 **依据 1 · 源码核查**：[package.json:1-12](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market/blob/19641d22a69b63063bb9b67a5f67a0dcb72703a0/package.json#L1-L12) 根名称、版本、服务入口与MIT声明。

        "answer": "变更锁在市场进程内串行 mutation，drain 通过 WeakMap 保存内部 probe/execute 身份，客户端不能在普通 body 中冒充。排空协调器实际接 Agent created/disposed/status 和 commands.cancelActive；要求两种生命周期订阅都可用，在每次实际包命令前再枚举/claim Agent，存在 unheld、取消、服务不可用或 barrier broken 就拒绝。这不等于跨进程锁，也不限制用户外部终端同时改同一 profile。\n\n维护 hold 丢失有条件处理：若 signal.reason.kind 为 disposed，代表会话关闭，删除hold并唤醒等待，不误取消包操作；其他丢失在 running/verifying 时打破 barrier 并请求取消。不能沿用“任何 hold 丢失都取消”的泛化。取消普通CLI会 killTree，Desktop交给 manager cancel；本地状态可能已经改变，安装/更新的取消故意让人看差异，不承诺事务回滚。\n\n本地 restore 路由确实受同源与变更锁保护，调用 restoreBackup 后先逐文件恢复，再把目标既有依赖与备份合并、执行 install；restoreProfileBackup 验路径/父目录并 temp+rename，一旦异常按 previous 还原。这是每文件替换与补偿，非整个profile崩溃原子，也不备份任意外部插件副作用或保全所有凭据。restoreBackup 首次 install 失败后还会清空依赖逐个重装，部分成功时返回 errors 并保留可装项，全部失败才回滚；因此HTTP ok或文件恢复完成也不等于备份全部恢复。本轮不审云上传备份链。\n\ndrain.ndjson 明确只存终态报告，等待操作不跨宿主重启复活。它与另一条 Desktop interrupted-update journal 不同：当前入口启动定时调用 repairPendingUpdates，runtime 确实交给 repairInterruptedUpdates；后者按实际安装版本判断，三次尝试后放弃自动修复，需要人工处理，不能写成所有操作没有持久恢复，也不能承诺任意重启都自愈。",

      "path": "README.md",
      "content": "<p align=\"center\">\n  <img src=\"assets/logo.svg\" width=\"96\" alt=\"dsh-market logo\">\n</p>\n\n# dsh-market\n\nEnglish | [中文](README.zh.md)\n\n[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dshmarket)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dshmarket)\n[![stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/dsh-market/dsh-market?style=flat)](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market)\n\nThe plugin market inside DeepSeek Harness. On dsh 0.2.1+ it is a tab on the **Plugins** page, right next to **Installed**; on older hosts open Settings → **Plugin Market**. Browse, search, one-click install.\n\n> 📡 **The same catalog is also a plugin market index.** On dsh 0.2.1+, open **Plugins → Discover → Index sources** and add `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/dsh-plugin-catalog/index.json`. That is this list as a format-1 index, served from npm so it loads quickly everywhere — dsh gives a source 15 seconds, and the GitHub Pages copies (`https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/index.json` and `https://dshmarket.com/index.json`) can exceed that from some networks. The host's Discover tab and the `plugin_market` agent tool then search it.\n\n![dsh-market](assets/demo-en.png)\n\nOne-click themes: install, switch live, no restart.\n\n## Install\n\n- **Official DSH Desktop:** Open **Settings → Plugins** in the app, search for\n  `dshmarket`, and install it through the app's plugin manager. No command line\n  is needed.\n- **Regular `dsh web`:** Run this command, then restart `dsh web`:\n\n  ```sh\n  dsh plugin --profile web add dshmarket\n  ```\n\n- **Custom profile:** Replace `web` in that command with your host's actual\n  profile name: `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dshmarket`. Follow your\n  host's restart instructions.\n\n- **From the GitHub source (no build):** `add github:dsh-market/dsh-market`\n  makes pnpm ask before running the package's build scripts. The prebuilt\n  tarball attached to the same release installs without that step:\n\n  ```sh\n  dsh plugin --profile <profile> add https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market/releases/download/v<version>/dshmarket-<version>.tgz\n  ```\n\nOn a machine with DSH Desktop, running `dsh plugin --profile web add dshmarket`\nmay report success but installs the market into `profiles/web`, **not** the\nprofile used by the Desktop app. It will not appear in Desktop. Install through\nthe app's **Settings → Plugins** instead; Desktop's profile is managed by the app.\n\nOnce it is installed, open the **Plugins** page and pick the **Plugin Market**\ntab next to **Installed** (dsh 0.2.1 and newer — plain `dsh web` included, no\ndesktop app needed). The market is also still a section of **Settings → Plugin\nMarket**: on dsh 0.2.0 and older that is the only way in, and from 0.2.1 the\nSettings dialog lives in the account menu. If you would rather reach it in one\nclick from anywhere, the market can also put its own **Plugin Market** row in\nthe sidebar; turn it on from the market's card under **Plugins**. All three\nentries can be switched individually under **Advanced** in that card, and the\nmarket refuses to close the last one. Going the\nother way, an installed plugin's **···** menu offers **View in Plugins** on\ndsh 0.2.1+: it opens the host's own page for that plugin, which is the only\nplace its individual rows can be switched one by one.\n\n**Requires dsh web 0.1.0-rc.6 or newer.** On an older host the market\ndisables itself and says so in the browser console rather than rendering\nagainst primitives that are not there — if the Plugin Market entry never\nappears, that is usually why. Worth checking when a desktop build bundles\nits own dsh: it may be older than the one `npm` would give you (#139).\n\n## What you get\n\n- **Browse & search** the full community catalog (4200+ plugins, growing daily) — category filters, star counts, top/new sorting, bilingual descriptions that follow your UI language\n- **Host-aware discovery** — cards show the DSH requirement declared by `engines.dsh` or lockstep `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peers; the compatibility filter hides only confirmed mismatches with the running host. GitHub-only entries read the linked package's manifest, including monorepo subdirectories; Release downloads read the selected release tag, including the current tag behind `latest/download`. Undeclared, malformed or unavailable requirements stay unknown and visible. Public manifest facts are cached; compatibility is evaluated against the running host\n- **Screenshots** — AppStore-style screenshots, auto-carousel when there's more than one, click to preview full-size: author-curated shots show right on the card (zero extra requests); plugins without curated shots fall back to automatic README extraction once you open the install dialog. Images load from GitHub hosting only\n- **Comments** — every card opens the plugin's discussion thread in place. It is the same thread its pages on [dshmarket.com](https://dshmarket.com) and the [catalog](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com) show, so a plugin has one conversation rather than three. Backed by GitHub Discussions through giscus: it loads when you open it, needs a GitHub account only to post, and the note above it says plainly that opening it contacts giscus.app and GitHub. On local dsh web, reading stays embedded while a dedicated GitHub action opens the exact discussion in a new tab for sign-in and posting, so the cross-site return never carries or depends on the host session\n- **Favorites** — bookmark plugins and themes from Discover or the Themes tab; a dedicated Favorites tab lists them with search, sort, and install actions. Bookmarks persist in the profile's market state (`state.json`); entries that leave the catalog can be cleared in one click\n- **Groups** — organise installed plugins into named groups (rename, delete, and per-group search); a plugin lives in one group and ungrouped is the default. A group carries its own switch: all-on, all-off, or the mixed state its members are really in, so a working set can be switched as a unit without touching the rest. A group holds at most one theme. The grouping itself is local state in the profile's `state.json`\n- **Notes** — write your own one-line description for any installed plugin and it replaces the author's on that row, so a shelf of forty plugins answers \"why did I install this\" in your words. Stored locally beside groups and favorites, never sent anywhere\n- **Themes** — a dedicated tab for community themes and skins: install → active immediately, switch with one click (themes are mutually exclusive, your choice survives restarts), uninstall to revert\n- **One-click install** — confirm the source, watch live progress; most plugins go live after a page refresh, no restart\n- **Backup & restore** — export your profile's plugin list and configuration as readable JSON, import it on another machine, store it on WebDAV with daily auto-backup, or sync through a private GitHub Gist; restores **merge** (plugins installed after the backup are kept), validate before writing, and roll back on failure\n- **Updates** — per-plugin update checks (npm version or pinned commit vs HEAD), one-click update, or update everything at once; the market updates itself the same way. A plugin installed from an archive link is updated only through its own source: a catalog entry that merely shares the name is never offered as its update, so updating cannot silently replace it with a different plugin. Each row with an update pending carries a **What changed** link — the release notes, or the commits when the version cannot be aligned to one. A notice you are not acting on can be ignored for the rest of the boot instead of being dismissed again on every reload — scoped to the running host, so a restart brings the reminder back and ignoring it is never the same as turning it off\n- **Resilient GitHub routes** — in the China download region, Git refs, README content, and avatars each keep their own fallback order. The market remembers the last working route, switches only after transport/HTTP/payload validation fails, and rejects proxy error pages disguised as HTTP 200.       "path": "src/drain-journal.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * Terminal-only journal for deferred plugin operations (#411).\n *\n * A deferred mutation is deliberately not durable across a Host restart: the\n * maintenance holds and the package command die with the process. What has to\n * survive is the *report* — \"the install you started last time failed\" — so a\n * user coming back after a restart is not left guessing. This file stores\n * exactly the bounded terminal facts: id, kind, package name, state, Agent\n * counts and time. No prompts, transcripts, tool input, environment values, or\n * paths.\n */\n\nimport { appendFileSync, closeSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, openSync, readFileSync, readSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'\nimport { dirname } from 'node:path'\nimport type { DrainJournalLike, DrainJournalRecord, DrainKind, DrainTerminalState } from './drain.ts'\nimport { redactHomePaths } from './log-redaction.ts'\n\nconst MAX_BYTES = 64 * 1024\nconst MAX_RECORDS = 50\nconst TEXT_MAX = 200\n\nconst KINDS: ReadonlySet<DrainKind> = new Set(['install', 'update', 'uninstall'])\nconst STATES: ReadonlySet<DrainTerminalState> = new Set(['succeeded', 'failed', 'cancelled'])\n\nfunction clean(value: unknown, max = TEXT_MAX): string | null {\n  if (typeof value !== 'string') return null\n  const text = redactHomePaths(value).replace(/[\\u0000-\\u001f\\u007f]/g, ' ').trim()\n  return text === '' ? null : text.slice(0, max)\n}\n\nfunction parseLine(line: string): DrainJournalRecord | null {\n  let value: unknown\n  try {\n    value = JSON.parse(line) as unknown\n  } catch {\n    return null\n  }\n  if (value === null || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) return null\n  const row = value as Record<string, unknown>\n  const id = clean(row.id)\n  const name = clean(row.name)\n  const kind = row.kind\n  const state = row.state\n  if (id === null || name === null) return null\n  if (typeof kind !== 'string' || !KINDS.has(kind as DrainKind)) return null\n  if (typeof state !== 'string' || !STATES.has(state as DrainTerminalState)) return null\n  if (typeof row.at !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(row.at)) return null\n  if (typeof row.agentsAtStart !== 'number' || typeof row.agentsAtEnd !== 'number') return null\n  return {\n    at: row.at,\n    id,\n    kind: kind as DrainKind,\n    name,\n    state: state as DrainTerminalState,\n    agentsAtStart: row.agentsAtStart,\n    agentsAtEnd: row.agentsAtEnd,\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether the file is empty or its last byte is a newline — i.e. whether an\n * append starts a line of its own. Reads one byte rather than the file: this\n * runs on every completed operation, and the journal is bounded but not tiny.\n */\nfunction endsWithNewline(file: string): boolean {\n  try {\n    const size = statSync(file).size\n    if (size === 0) return true\n    const fd = openSync(file, 'r')\n    try {\n      const last = Buffer.alloc(1)\n      readSync(fd, last, 0, 1, size - 1)\n      return last[0] === 0x0a\n    } finally {\n      closeSync(fd)\n    }\n  } catch {\n    // No file yet (a fresh append creates it) or unreadable: appending a\n    // leading newline to a missing file would only add a blank line.\n    return true\n  }\n}\n\nexport class DrainJournal implements DrainJournalLike {\n  private readonly file: string\n  private readonly maxBytes: number\n  private records: DrainJournalRecord[] = []\n\n  constructor(file: string, maxBytes = MAX_BYTES) {\n    this.file = file\n    this.maxBytes = maxBytes\n    this.load()\n  }\n\n  /** Append one terminal record; the in-memory copy survives a write failure. */\n  append(record: DrainJournalRecord): void {\n    const cleaned: DrainJournalRecord = {\n      at: record.at,\n      id: clean(record.id) ?? 'drain',\n      kind: record.kind,\n      name: clean(record.name) ?? 'plugin',\n      state: record.state,\n      agentsAtStart: Number.isFinite(record.agentsAtStart) ? record.agentsAtStart : 0,\n      agentsAtEnd: Number.isFinite(record.agentsAtEnd) ? record.agentsAtEnd : 0,\n    }\n    this.records.push(cleaned)\n    if (this.records.length > MAX_RECORDS) this.records.splice(0, this.records.length - MAX_RECORDS)\n    mkdirSync(dirname(this.file), { recursive: true })\n    // An interrupted write leaves a tail without its newline. Appending to it\n    // would glue this record onto the damaged one, so the file would carry a\n    // single unparseable line and BOTH would be lost on reopen — the record\n    // this append just completed included (#1084). The damaged tail is\n    // dropped by load() on its own; this only keeps the next record separate.\n    appendFileSync(this.file, `${endsWithNewline(this.file) ? '' : '\\n'}${JSON.stringify(cleaned)}\\n`)\n    if (existsSync(this.file) && statSync(this.file).size > this.maxBytes) this.trim()\n  }\n\n  /** The newest terminal records, oldest first. */\n  recent(max = 10): DrainJournalRecord[] {\n    return this.records.slice(-max).map(record => ({ ...record }))\n  }\n\n  private load(): void {\n    try {\n      if (!existsSync(this.file)) return\n      const parsed: DrainJournalRecord[] = []\n      for (const line of readFileSync(this.file, 'utf8').split('\\n')) {\n        if (line === '') continue\n        const record = parseLine(line)\n        if (record !== null) parsed.push(record)\n      }\n      this.records = parsed.slice(-MAX_RECORDS)\n      if (statSync(this.file).size > this.maxBytes) this.trim()\n    } catch {\n      // An unreadable journal is a lost report, not a broken market.\n      this.records = []\n    }\n  }\n\n  /** Keep the newest half, matching the persistent log's trim discipline. */\n  private trim(): void {\n    try {\n      const lines = readFileSync(this.file, 'utf8').split('\\n').filter(line => line !== '')\n      const kept: string[] = []\n      let bytes = 0\n      for (let index = lines.length - 1; index >= 0 && bytes <= this.maxBytes / 2; index -= 1) {\n        kept.unshift(`${lines[index]!}\\n`)\n        bytes += lines[index]!.length + 1\n      }\n      writeFileSync(this.file, kept.join(''))\n      this.records = kept\n        .map(line => parseLine(line.trimEnd()))\n        .filter((record): record is DrainJournalRecord => record !== null)\n    } catch {\n      // Leave the file as it is; the in-memory tail still serves this process.\n    }\n  }\n}\n"

      "content": "/**\n * Host-owned coordinator for Agent-safe deferred plugin mutations (#411).\n *\n * The safety invariant is #199's: plugin files must not be replaced or\n * removed while an Agent can still execute a turn against them. Existing turns are allowed to finish; nothing here calls\n * `Agent.cancel()`.\n *\n * One process-local coordinator owns one deferred operation at a time, every\n * maintenance hold, and the operation record the browser projects. The record\n * carries counts and ids only — never prompts, transcripts, tool input, or\n * paths (FR-11).\n */\n\nimport { drainableAgent, type DrainableAgent } from './agents.ts'\nimport { redactHomePaths } from './log-redaction.ts'\n\nexport type DrainKind = 'install' | 'update' | 'uninstall'\n\nexport type DrainState =\n  | 'accepted'\n  | 'draining'\n  | 'queued-for-mutation'\n  | 'running'\n  | 'verifying'\n  | 'succeeded'\n  | 'failed'\n  | 'cancelled'\n\nexport type DrainTerminalState = 'succeeded' | 'failed' | 'cancelled'\n\n/** Why the operation is queued. Only `agents` exists in v1. */\nexport interface DrainWait {\n  reason: 'agents'\n  /**\n   * Agents the operation is waiting on: those in a turn or, when none is, every\n   * live Agent not yet maintenance-held. Refreshed when the drain loop wakes,\n   * so it can lag behind a turn that just ended or started.\n   */\n  activeCount: number\n  /** Their local session ids. With a turn running, the same ids as a 409's `runningAgents`. */\n  activeAgentIds: string[]\n  since: number\n}\n\n/** The immutable facts a delayed operation may not silently change. */\nexport interface DrainExpectation {\n  /** install/update: the exact pnpm target (version, commit, or tarball). */\n  target?: string\n  /** update/uninstall: the installed spec the operation was approved against. */\n  spec?: string\n  /** update/uninstall: the installed version baseline, when readable. */\n  version?: string | null\n}\n\nexport interface DrainIntent {\n  kind: DrainKind\n  /** Package name, or the catalog name for an install. */\n  name: string\n  /** Catalog url, present for installs. */\n  url?: string\n  expected: DrainExpectation\n}\n\nexport interface DrainFailure {\n  code: string\n  message: string\n}\n\n/** Bounded terminal facts the client needs to drive its existing banners. */\nexport interface DrainOutcome {\n  needsRefresh: boolean\n  restartRequired: boolean\n  activation: string | null\n  hot: boolean\n}\n\n/** The browser-facing projection of one operation. */\nexport interface DrainOperationView {\n  operationId: string\n  kind: DrainKind\n  name: string\n  url?: string\n  state: DrainState\n  createdAt: number\n  startedAt: number | null\n  finishedAt: number | null\n  wait: DrainWait | null\n  failure: DrainFailure | null\n  outcome: DrainOutcome | null\n}\n\n/** The result of re-running the route's ordinary executor. */\nexport interface DrainExecutionResult {\n  status: number\n  payload: unknown\n}\n\n/** Why the executor may not touch the profile right now. */\nexport type DrainMutationReason =\n  | 'market-unloaded'\n  | 'cancelled'\n  | 'barrier-broken'\n  | 'agents-service-unavailable'\n  | 'agent-active'\n\nexport type DrainMutationGate =\n  | { ok: true }\n  | { ok: false; reason: DrainMutationReason; ids: string[] }\n\nexport interface DrainJournalRecord {\n  at: number\n  id: string\n  kind: DrainKind\n  name: string\n  state: DrainTerminalState\n  agentsAtStart: number\n  agentsAtEnd: number\n}\n\nexport interface DrainJournalLike {\n  append(record: DrainJournalRecord): void\n}\n\n/**\n * What the coordinator needs from the host.\n *\n * `list()` returns null when the host has no readable `agents` service.\n * The event methods return null when this host cannot report Agent creation\n * and disposal;       "content": "/**\n * Install orchestration: collection-repo retargeting, post-install\n * validation that keeps broken pieces from bricking the next boot, and\n * update staleness detection. Every function takes the plugin runner as a\n * parameter so tests can substitute a recording fake.\n */\n\nimport { closeSync, existsSync, lstatSync, openSync, readFileSync, readlinkSync, readSync, rmSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'\nimport { dirname, isAbsolute, join, resolve } from 'node:path'\nimport type { InstallResult, PluginRunner } from './dsh-cli.ts'\nimport { findDshInstallDir } from './dsh-install.ts'\nimport { classifyPnpmFailure, HOST_NAMESPACE_RE, isTransientPnpmFailure } from './pnpm-compat.ts'\nimport { conflictingEntryIds, dropFromManifest, hasDshManifest, hasLoadableEntry, mergeDuplicateReleaseAgeExcludes, pluginSubdirs, profileDir, readGitResolutionCommit, readInstalled, readInstalledVersion, readLockCommits, readManifestDeps, readProfileBundles, dropUnparseableBuildKeys } from './profile.ts'\nimport { logEvent } from './log.ts'\nimport { registryNameOf } from './official-desktop.ts'\nimport { hostedRepoKey } from './sources.ts'\nimport { cleanOrphanedIgnored, cleanOrphanedStore } from './store.ts'\n\n/**\n * One-shot bypass for pnpm's fresh-release hold; scoped to a single command.\n *\n * Spelled like the .npmrc key, not the camelCase pnpm-workspace.yaml one:\n * from pnpm 12.3.0 (the native CLI) `--config.minimumReleaseAge=0` is\n * silently ignored — no unknown-option error — so the retry ran without the\n * bypass and failed exactly like the first attempt (#600).\n * `--config.minimum-release-age=0` is honoured by pnpm 10, 11 and 12 alike.\n * That is specific to this key, not a rule for `--config.*`: the native CLI\n * ignores `--config.fetch-timeout` in both spellings, which is why\n * FETCH_TIMEOUT_OVERRIDE below is not respelled here (#615).\n */\nexport const RELEASE_AGE_OVERRIDE = '--config.minimum-release-age=0'\n\n/**\n * Longer per-request fetch timeout for one retried command. pnpm's default\n * 60-second limit aborts large tarball downloads (github: sources fetch the\n * WHOLE repo even for a `#path:` subdirectory plugin) on slow networks; a\n * plain retry fails again at the same limit, so the recovery re-runs with\n * this override once. Scoped to a single command like RELEASE_AGE_OVERRIDE.\n *\n * pnpm 12 ignores this flag on the command line in either spelling (#615).\n * On the CLI runner, runDshPlugin repeats every `--config.<key>` override\n * as PNPM_CONFIG_<KEY>, which pnpm 11 and 12 both read, so the retried\n * command really does get the longer limit there. The Desktop runtime hands\n * its host argv only, so on a Desktop host the retry still depends on that\n * host's pnpm reading the flag. The flag stays: pnpm 11 and earlier read\n * it, and it costs nothing on the versions that do not.\n */\nexport const FETCH_TIMEOUT_OVERRIDE = '--config.fetchTimeout=600000'\n\n/**\n * Stop pnpm downloading a plugin's peer dependencies (#289 by @00080000).\n *\n * The last resort for a peer that cannot be downloaded because it does not\n * exist on any registry: the dsh runtime injects several `@deepseek-ai/*`\n * packages and never publishes them, and since pnpm 8 `auto-install-peers`\n * defaults on, so pnpm walks the peer list and 404s on one.\n *\n * Only on the retry, never by default. Turning it off wholesale would also\n * stop pnpm installing the peers a plugin legitimately needs from npm, and\n * that failure would surface much later — as a missing module at runtime\n * rather than a clear error at install time. Narrow beats early here.\n *\n * Verified against pnpm 10.29.3: `peerDependencyRules.ignoreMissing` does\n * NOT prevent the fetch (it only silences the warning), so this flag is the\n * only lever that actually works.\n *\n * pnpm 12 ignores this flag on the command line too (12.4.1 auto-installs\n * the peer regardless); runDshPlugin repeats it as\n * PNPM_CONFIG_AUTO_INSTALL_PEERS, which 12 reads (#615).\n */\nexport const AUTO_INSTALL_PEERS_OFF = '--config.auto-install-peers=false'\n\n/**\n * Whether an unresolvable package is a host peer pnpm went looking for on\n * its own, rather than something the profile actually asks for.\n *\n * The same 404 means two different things and wants two different answers.\n * A `@deepseek-ai/*` package that IS in the profile manifest is a ghost\n * entry — left by an earlier failed operation, or hand-added — and the user\n * has to remove that line; retrying would only fail again. One that is NOT\n * in the manifest was never asked for by anybody: pnpm reached it by walking\n * an installed plugin's peerDependencies, which in this ecosystem name what\n * the runtime provides rather than what npm carries.\n *\n * Reading the manifest is what separates them, so this cannot live in the\n * pure classifier.\n */\nexport function isUnpublishedHostPeer(\n  pkg: string | undefined,\n  profile: string,\n  explicitDir?: string,\n): boolean {\n  if (pkg === undefined || !HOST_NAMESPACE_RE.test(pkg)) return false\n  return !Object.hasOwn(readManifestDeps(profile, explicitDir), pkg)\n}\n\n/**\n * Run one plugin command with automatic recovery from three known pnpm traps:\n *\n * - pnpm-major drift (#20 bug 2): a modules directory built by a different\n *   pnpm major fails mutation; pnpm's documented remedy is one `install` to\n *   recreate it — do that silently and retry the original command once.\n * - release-age lockfile lock (#39): once a too-young release is in the\n *   lockfile, pnpm 11 rejects EVERY later add/remove during verification —\n *   retry once with the one-shot minimumReleaseAge bypass (safe: the young\n *   package is already installed; the bypass only lets pnpm touch the\n *   lockfile again).\n * - per-request fetch timeout: large tarballs (github: sources fetch the\n *   whole repo even for a `#path:` subdirectory) on slow networks blow\n *   pnpm's default 60-second limit; a plain retry fails again at the same\n *   limit, so retry once with a longer fetchTimeout.\n *\n * Any recognized failure that survives gets its bilingual explanation\n * appended to stderr so the UI shows an actionable message instead of a\n * wall of text (#20 bug 3). Cancelled runs are never recovered.\n *\n * The release-age bypass can be declined (`releaseAgeBypass: false`). Its\n * safety argument above assumes the young package is already installed; a\n * fresh install pinned to the registry's latest (#594) is the one case\n * where it is not — there the bypass would be what installs the young\n * version, over a minimumReleaseAge the profile set on purpose — so the\n * install route declines it and falls back to the bare name instead.\n *\n * `marketFlags: false` says the host runs pnpm itself and takes no options\n * from us (the official Desktop bridge, #732). The four recoveries below\n * each decorate a command with an option, so on such a host they are skipped\n * rather than sent and refused — and because their classifier messages say\n * the market retried, the note appended at the end says it did not.\n */\nexport async function withHoistRecovery(\n  run: PluginRunner,\n  profile: string,\n  pluginArgs: string[],\n  profileDirectory?: string,\n  options: { releaseAgeBypass?: boolean; marketFlags?: boolean; preserveProfilePolicy?: boolean } = {},\n): Promise<InstallResult> {\n  const marketFlags = options.marketFlags !== false\n  // An already verified mature update must not rewrite the user's workspace\n  // policy as a side effect of market-level recovery (#991).\n  const repairProfilePolicy = options.preserveProfilePolicy !== true\n  /** The option a recovery step needed and this host does not accept (#732). */\n  let unavailableOption: string | null = null\n  // Before the FIRST run, not after a failure: the shadowed duplicate rule\n  // (#732) hurts pnpm while it RESOLVES the dependency graph, so merging it\n  // first is what keeps the command from failing at all — and it costs one\n  // small file read. Every verb that resolves the graph is covered, not just\n  // add and remove: an `install` or an in-place `update` reads the same key.\n  const verb = pluginArgs.find(argument => !argument.startsWith('-'))\n  if (repairProfilePolicy && (verb === 'add' || verb === 'remove' || verb === 'install' || verb === 'update')) {\n    const merged = mergeDuplicateReleaseAgeExcludes(profile, profileDirectory)\n    if (merged.length > 0) {\n      logEvent('warn', 'install', `minimumReleaseAgeExclude held several rules for ${merged.join(', ')}, and pnpm honours only the FIRST per name (#732) — merged each package's rules into one, before running`)\n    }\n  }\n  let result = await run(profile, pluginArgs)\n  const ok = (r: InstallResult): boolean => r.exitCode === 0 && !r.timedOut && !r.cancelled\n  // A shadowed rule written DURING the run is its own evidence (#732). The\n  // file was merged just before the run, so a duplicate now means pnpm — or\n  // the host driving it — appended one while this command ran, and every\n  // retry would trip on it. The repair below in the release-age branch only\n  // fired when pnpm's error text reached us; the official desktop host hands\n  // back its own message and `packageResult.output`, which need not carry\n  // `ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION`, so the line the host had just\n  // appended stayed dead (@Mlte0907, 1.66.7). The merge is a no-op when\n  // nothing is duplicated, so asking it costs one file read.\n  let repairedDuringRun = false\n  if (repairProfilePolicy && !ok(result) && !result.cancelled && (pluginArgs[0] === 'add' || pluginArgs[0] === 'remove')) {\n    const mergedNow = mergeDuplicateReleaseAgeExcludes(profile, profileDirectory)\n    if (mergedNow.length > 0) {\n      repairedDuringRun = true\n      logEvent('warn', 'install', `a second minimumReleaseAgeExclude rule for ${mergedNow.join(', ')} was appended during the run, and pnpm honours only the first, shadowing it (#732) — merged them into one and retrying once`)\n      result = await run(profile, pluginArgs)\n    }\n  }\n  if (!ok(result) && !result.cancelled && !repairedDuringRun) {\n    // The profile is the only place the recorded pnpm major lives (#1100).\n    const failure = classifyPnpmFailure(`${result.stderr}\\n${result.stdout}`, result.exitCode, { profileDirectory })\n    if (failure?.code === 'unparseable-build-key' && repairProfilePolicy) {\n      // The profile's own allowBuilds block is what fails, so no retry of the\n      // same command can pass until it is repaired (#698). Drop only the\n      // source-form keys this pnpm cannot parse — bare names stay, and on\n      // these versions a bare name is what authorizes a git dependency — then\n      // run the command once more.\n      const removed = dropUnparseableBuildKeys(profile, profileDirectory)\n      if (removed.length > 0) {\n        logEvent('warn', 'install', `this pnpm cannot parse git-source allowBuilds keys; removed ${removed.join(', ')} from pnpm-workspace.yaml and retrying once (#698)`)\n        result = await run(profile, pluginArgs)\n      }\n    } else if (failure?.code === 'hoist-pattern-diff') {\n      if (!marketFlags) {\n        unavailableOption = '--no-frozen-lockfile'\n      } else {\n        logEvent('warn', 'install', `modules dir was built by a different pnpm major — rebuilding (pnpm install) and retrying once`)\n        // --no-frozen-lockfile: the market runs pnpm with CI=true (TTY hangs),\n        // where a lockfile written by the old major would otherwise be refused.\n        const rebuild = await run(profile, ['install', '--no-frozen-lockfile'])\n        if (ok(rebuild)) result = await run(profile, pluginArgs)\n      }\n    } else if (\n      failure?.code === 'release-age-violation'\n      && (pluginArgs[0] === 'add' || pluginArgs[0] === 'remove')\n    ) {\n      // The repair ran before this command, so a rewrite here means pnpm wrote\n      // one of the two broken shapes DURING it — appending a shadowed rule\n      // (#732) or extending a version union (#733). Either way the same\n      // rewrite fixes it, needs no option at all, and so also works on the\n      // desktop bridge that refuses options. Retry the SAME argv afterwards.\n      const mergedNow = repairProfilePolicy ? mergeDuplicateReleaseAgeExcludes(profile, profileDirectory) : []\n      if (mergedNow.length > 0) {\n        logEvent('warn', 'install', `pnpm appended a second minimumReleaseAgeExclude rule for ${mergedNow.join(', ')} and honours only the first, shadowing its own entry (#732) — merged them into one and retrying once`)\n        result = await run(profile, pluginArgs)\n      } else if (options.releaseAgeBypass === false || options.preserveProfilePolicy === true) {\n        // Fresh installs (#594) and mature updates/recovery (#991) never\n        // bypass age enforcement. Preserve the native failure and policy.\n      } else if (!marketFlags) {\n        unavailableOption = RELEASE_AGE_OVERRIDE\n      } else if (pluginArgs.includes(RELEASE_AGE_OVERRIDE)) {\n        // Already carrying it (a caller's forced retry): nothing left to add.\n      } else {\n        logEvent('warn', 'install', `a too-young release blocks pnpm's lockfile verification (#39) — retrying once with ${RELEASE_AGE_OVERRIDE}`)\n        result = await run(profile, [pluginArgs[0], RELEASE_AGE_OVERRIDE, ...pluginArgs.slice(1)])\n      }\n    } else if (\n      (failure?.code === 'fetch-404' || failure?.code === 'no-matching-version')\n      && isUnpublishedHostPeer(failure.pkg, profile, profileDirectory)\n      && (pluginArgs[0] === 'add' || pluginArgs[0] === 'remove')\n      && !pluginArgs.includes(AUTO_INSTALL_PEERS_OFF)\n    ) {\n      // The plugin is fine; pnpm went looking for a package the host injects\n      // and npm has never carried. Every fresh profile hits this, whatever\n      // the plugin, so failing here would be failing for something the user\n      // cannot fix and did not cause.\n      if (!marketFlags) {\n        unavailableOption = AUTO_INSTALL_PEERS_OFF\n      } else {\n        logEvent('warn', 'install', `${failure.pkg ?? 'a host package'} is a peer the runtime provides and npm does not carry (#289) — retrying once with ${AUTO_INSTALL_PEERS_OFF}`)\n        result = await run(profile, [pluginArgs[0], AUTO_INSTALL_PEERS_OFF, ...pluginArgs.slice(1)])\n      }\n    } else if (failure?.code === 'profile-file-locked') {\n      // #786 follow-up: the profile's own file was momentarily held, so the\n      // SAME argv succeeds — no option is needed, which also means this works\n      // on the desktop bridge that refuses market options (#732).\n      //\n      // Covers both lockfiles pnpm writes through the same no-retry atomic\n      // rename: the profile's `pnpm-lock.yaml` and the one inside\n      // `node_modules/.pnpm/lock.yaml`.\n      //\n      // Retried here rather than in the route because `pnpmBlockedByOpenFiles`\n      // and the route's rollback both read the FINAL result: leaving this\n      // unretried made the route treat a transient lock as \"the running host\n      // holds the plugin's files open\", restore package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml\n      // — and thereby throw away a lockfile that already pointed at the newly\n      // built commit, which is what left the profile desynchronized.\n      logEvent('warn', 'install', `pnpm was momentarily refused on a profile file (antivirus or indexer) — retrying the same command once (#786)`)\n      result = await run(profile, pluginArgs)\n    } else if (failure?.code === 'transient-network'\n      && (pluginArgs[0] === 'add' || pluginArgs[0] === 'remove')\n    ) {\n      // #83: pnpm replays the whole tree, so any existing dependency's\n      // momentary network hiccup fails the run — and a plain retry succeeds.\n      // Do that retry ourselves instead of reporting a false failure.\n      logEvent('warn', 'install', `transient network failure while pnpm replayed the dependency tree (#83) — retrying once`)\n      result = await run(profile, pluginArgs)\n    } else if (\n      failure?.code === 'exact-version-missing'\n      && (pluginArgs[0] === 'add' || pluginArgs[0] === 'remove' || pluginArgs[0] === 'update')\n    ) {\n      // #927: market pinned name@x.y.z from /latest, but this registry's\n      // packument (often a mirror) does not list that version yet. Same argv\n      // once more gives pnpm a chance to re-fetch; if it still fails the\n      // classifier's message names \"try later / switch Download region\".\n      logEvent('warn', 'install', `exact version missing on this registry's packument (#927) — retrying once to re-fetch`)\n      result = await run(profile, pluginArgs)\n    } else if (\n      failure?.code === 'fetch-timeout'\n      && (pluginArgs[0] === 'add' || pluginArgs[0] === 'remove')\n      && !pluginArgs.includes(FETCH_TIMEOUT_OVERRIDE)\n    ) {\n      // Large tarball / slow network: pnpm's default 60s per-request limit\n      // aborted the download. A plain retry fails again at the same limit,\n      // so retry once with a longer fetchTimeout.\n      if (!marketFlags) {\n        unavailableOption = FETCH_TIMEOUT_OVERRIDE\n      } else {\n        logEvent('warn', 'install', `pnpm's per-request fetch timeout aborted a large download — retrying once with ${FETCH_TIMEOUT_OVERRIDE}`)\n        result = await run(profile, [pluginArgs[0], FETCH_TIMEOUT_OVERRIDE, ...pluginArgs.slice(1)])\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  if (!ok(result) && !result.cancelled) {\n    // A failed, timed-out, or killed run never finishes pnpm's staging, so\n    // its store tmp dirs (the WHOLE repo tarball for github: sources) are\n    // orphaned — reclaim them now that no pnpm is running. Safe by\n    // construction: directories are only removed when their owning pid is\n    // gone (the name carries it), so a live download is never touched.\n    await cleanOrphanedStore(run, profile)\n    const diagnostics = diagnosticsTail(result)\n    const failure = classifyPnpmFailure(`${result.stderr}\\n${result.stdout}`, result.exitCode, { profileDirectory })\n    if (failure !== null) {\n      result = {\n        ...result,\n        stderr: failure.replaceOutput === true ? failure.message : `${result.stderr}\\n\\n${failure.message}`,\n        ...(failure.replaceOutput === true ? { stdout: '' } : {}),\n      }\n    } else {\n      // Nothing matched. Two things may still say what went wrong, and pnpm's\n      // own words come FIRST (#808).\n      //\n      // pnpm's structured error arrives in its ndjson stream, which never\n      // reaches stderr. Without it the user sees the tail of dsh's wrapper\n      // output (\"pnpm failed in profile directory …\"), byte-identical for\n      // every possible cause — why #244, #192 and #138 all read as \"the UI\n      // shows a stack tail\". An unrecognized error is where the raw text is\n      // worth the most: a classified one has a written explanation, this one\n      // has only pnpm's own words.\n      //\n      // The CLI's diagnostics file (`dsh: pnpm failed; diagnostics: <path>`,\n      // #672) used to carry the whole pnpm run. It no longer does: dsh now\n      // pipes pnpm's output straight to the market, and the file keeps only\n      // execa's one-line summary (\"Command failed with exit code 1: pnpm add\n      // …\"). Showing it INSTEAD of pnpm's error — which is what an either/or\n      // here did — put that summary in front of the user and hid the real\n      // cause behind it. Its path is still worth printing for a report, so it\n      // stays, after the error.\n      const blocks: string[] = []\n      if (result.pnpmError !== undefined && result.pnpmError !== '') {\n        const code = result.pnpmErrorCode === undefined ? '' : `${result.pnpmErrorCode}: `\n        blocks.push(`${code}${result.pnpmError}`)\n      }\n      if (diagnostics !== null) blocks.push(`--- dsh diagnostics (${diagnostics.path}) ---\\n${diagnostics.text}`)\n      if (blocks.length > 0) result = { ...result, stderr: `${result.stderr}\\n\\n${blocks.join('\\n\\n')}` }\n    }\n  }\n  if (!marketFlags && !ok(result) && !result.cancelled\n    && classifyPnpmFailure(`${result.stderr}\\n${result.stdout}`, result.exitCode)?.code === 'windows-file-locked') {\n    // The classified text offers \"run it from the command line with the app\n    // closed\". On the official desktop app that is the one thing the market\n    // does not do for the user — it never falls back to `dsh plugin --profile\n    // desktop`, which is forbidden there — so the advice sent the reporter to a\n    // door the market itself keeps shut (#798). Say what to do instead: the\n    // app's own Plugins page runs the same managed pipeline.\n    //\n    // Not for the market itself: Settings → Plugins has no update entry for a\n    // package already in the profile (#909). That note would send a self-update\n    // to a shut door (#982).\n    const lockedTarget = pluginArgs.find(argument => !argument.startsWith('-') && argument !== verb) ?? ''\n    const lockedName = registryNameOf(lockedTarget) ?? lockedTarget\n    if (lockedName !== 'dshmarket' && lockedName !== 'dsh-market') {\n      result = {\n        ...result,\n        stderr: `${result.stderr}\\n\\n这是官方桌面端：上面「在命令行执行」这一条在这里用不了，请改在应用自己的「设置 → 插件」里操作（退出重启后，或先停用加载该包的插件再重启）。 / This is the official desktop app: the \"run it from the command line\" option above is not available here — use the app's own Settings → Plugins instead (after restarting, or after disabling the plugin that loads this package and restarting).`,\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  if (unavailableOption !== null && !ok(result) && !result.cancelled) {\n    // #732: this step was skipped because the host runs pnpm itself and takes\n    // no options from us — but the classified message above says the market\n    // retried. Say that it did not, or the user reads a retry that never\n    // happened and looks for the wrong cause.\n    //\n    // The wait on a fresh release is the one of these where \"no retry\" leaves\n    // the user with nothing to do at all: the plugin IS published, pnpm just\n    // will not take it yet. #852 pointed at plain `dsh web`, but the desktop\n    // profile is host-managed — that door is shut (#909). Say the wait, and\n    // when pnpm named the publish time, how long is left (#919).\n    //\n    // Drop the classifier's \"market already retried\" sentence first: it was\n    // appended above and is false on this host, and the client prefers\n    // body.error / that classified half over a note tacked on afterwards.\n    let note: string\n    if (unavailableOption === RELEASE_AGE_OVERRIDE) {\n      const classified = classifyPnpmFailure(`${result.stderr}\\n${result.stdout}`, result.exitCode)\n      if (classified?.code === 'release-age-violation') {\n        const cut = result.stderr.lastIndexOf(classified.message)\n        if (cut !== -1) {\n          result = { ...result, stderr: result.stderr.slice(0, cut).trimEnd() }\n        }\n      }\n      const windowMs = readMinimumReleaseAgeMs(profile, profileDirectory)\n      const captured = `${result.stderr}\\n${result.stdout}`\n      const remaining = windowMs === null\n        ? null\n        : remainingReleaseAgeWait(captured, Date.now(), windowMs)\n      const wait = remaining === null ? { zh: '', en: '' } : formatRemainingReleaseAgeWait(remaining)\n      // #944: pnpm verifies the WHOLE lockfile, so the entry it refuses need\n      // not be the one this command asked for. When it names a different\n      // package, saying \"this plugin's new version is too young\" is wrong\n      // twice over — it blames an innocent package, and it attaches the\n      // remaining wait to that package's version rather than the offender's.\n      // Name the offender instead, and offer the one-line remedy the reporter\n      // used in place of waiting. Nothing is claimed when the output names no\n      // package, or names the one being installed: that path keeps #919's note.\n      const target = pluginArgs.find(argument => !argument.startsWith('-') && argument !== verb) ?? ''\n      const targetName = registryNameOf(target) ?? target\n      const refused = refusedReleaseAgePackage(captured)\n      if (refused !== null && targetName !== '' && refused.name !== targetName) {\n        note = `拦住你的是 ${refused.name}@${refused.version}，不是你要装的这个插件：pnpm 在改动前校验整个 lockfile，而这个版本还在本机的新版本等待期内（#944）。官方桌面端不接受临时放行，所以这里没有自动重试。**等 ${refused.name}@${refused.version} 过了等待期再更新一次即可**${wait.zh}；想现在就装，在 profile 的 pnpm-workspace.yaml 里 minimumReleaseAgeExclude 中**这个名字的那一行**（没有就新增一行）追加 \\` || ${refused.version}\\`——带引号的行要加在引号里面。不要另开一行同名规则：pnpm 只读第一条（#883）。 / What is holding you is ${refused.name}@${refused.version}, not the plugin you asked to install: pnpm verifies the whole lockfile before any change, and that version is still inside this machine's fresh-release wait (#944). The official desktop app takes no one-shot bypass, so no automatic retry happens here. **Update again once ${refused.name}@${refused.version} is past the wait**${wait.en}; to install right now, append \\` || ${refused.version}\\` to the row for \\`${refused.name}\\` under minimumReleaseAgeExclude in the profile's pnpm-workspace.yaml — inside the quotes when the row is quoted, and in a new row only if none exists. Do not add a second row for the same name: pnpm reads only the first (#883).`\n      } else {\n        note = `这个插件的新版本比本机的新版本等待期还新，所以现在装不了（改别的插件也会被拦住）。官方桌面端不接受临时放行，所以这里没有自动重试。**等这个版本过了等待期再更新一次即可**${wait.zh}。过了等待期后再在市场点一次更新。 / The plugin's new version is younger than this machine's fresh-release wait, so the install was refused (a change to another plugin too). The official desktop app takes no one-shot bypass, so no automatic retry happens here. **Update again once the version is past the wait**${wait.en}. Try the market update again after the wait.`\n      }\n    } else {\n      note = `这台宿主（官方桌面端）自己执行安装，不接受市场附加的 pnpm 参数（${unavailableOption}），所以这一步没有自动重试。 / This host (the official desktop app) runs the install itself and takes no pnpm options from the market (${unavailableOption}), so that automatic retry could not be attempted.`\n    }\n    result = { ...result, stderr: `${result.stderr}\\n\\n${note}` }\n  }\n  // pnpm can append a second rule even on success (#883, #878), including\n  // after a recovery retry or an official Desktop manager install. Repair\n  // the final file now, before another plugin operation reads it; a successful\n  // command must never be retried just because its exclusions needed merging.\n  if (repairProfilePolicy && ok(result) && (verb === 'add' || verb === 'remove' || verb === 'install' || verb === 'update')) {\n    try {\n      const merged = mergeDuplicateReleaseAgeExcludes(profile, profileDirectory)\n      if (merged.length > 0) {\n        logEvent('warn', 'install', `merged duplicate minimumReleaseAgeExclude rules for ${merged.join(', ')} after success (#883, #878)`)\n      }\n    } catch (error) {\n      logEvent('warn', 'install', `could not merge minimumReleaseAgeExclude after success (#883, #878): ${String(error)}`)\n    }\n  }\n  // After every mutation — success, failure, and cancel. Garbage lands in\n  // `.ignored` on the NEXT pnpm run, so a success-only hook would miss the\n  // run that just moved it there (#974).
